canonical_topic: Leveling determination is a firm management judgment
definition: A statement that classifying a security's fair-value level is a discretionary determination made by each firm rather than a fixed, universal rule.
core_idea: Each firm's management decides how to level a given security, and that determination depends on what market data the firm itself has access to, so the same security could be leveled differently across firms and can change over time as data access changes.
key_points: The level assigned to a security is determined by each firm's own management.
The determination depends on the market data the firm has access to.
This designation can change over time as data access changes.
relationships: Applies generally to the level 1/2/3 hierarchy illustrated by the Henry Hub / Texas basis example.
trading_implications: Two firms holding economically identical positions could report different fair-value levels depending on their respective market data access.
caveats: Assuming fair-value leveling is an objective, firm-independent classification rather than a management judgment call.
